title: 14. Ensemble Learning & Boosting (XGBoost)
description: Compare Bagging vs Boosting, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost.

blocks.content:
### Bagging vs. Boosting

- **Bagging**: Trains models **in parallel** on random data subsets (reduces variance).
- **Boosting**: Trains models **sequentially**, where each model corrects residual errors of prior trees (reduces bias).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Boosting["Sequential Boosting Chain"]
        M1["Model 1"] -->|"Residual Errors"| M2["Model 2 (Focuses on Errors)"] -->|"Residual Errors"| M3["Model 3"]
    end
```

![Boosting Performance Comparison](/images/ml/chart_boosting_comparison.png)

blocks.starterCode:
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification

X, y = make_classification(n_samples=200, n_features=5, random_state=42)

gb = GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=50, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3)
gb.fit(X, y)
print(f'Training Score: {gb.score(X, y):.4f}')
blocks.solutionCode:
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification

X, y = make_classification(n_samples=200, n_features=5, random_state=42)
gb = GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=50, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3)
gb.fit(X, y)
print(f'Training Score: {gb.score(X, y):.4f}')
